paper.title: Efficient contextual partial monitoring with general function approximation

settings.name_in_paper: Contextual stochastic partial monitoring (partial monitoring with side information), globally observable games
unmapped: Outcome O_t drawn from q*(x_t) where q* belongs to a known realizable model class Q of context-to-outcome-distribution maps
Loss matrix L in [0,1]^{k x d} and feedback matrix Phi known to the learner; m feedback symbols, d outcomes
Game assumed non-degenerate with no duplicate actions
Regret against best action for each context (per-context comparator)
Algorithm requires an online outcome-estimation oracle with Hellinger regret bound
settings.definition_quote: At round $t$ the learner observes a context $x_t$ (which may be chosen adversarially), samples an action $A_t \sim p_t(\cdot \mid x_t)$ ... and the environment draws an outcome $O_t$ from some stochastic distribution $q^{\ast}(x_t)$ ... The learner then observes the feedback symbol $\sigma_t = \Phi_{A_t O_t}$ and incurs the loss $L_{A_t O_t}$, which remains hidden.

conditions: online oracle has Hellinger regret bound Reg_On w.p. 1-delta

source.label: theorem_doec_regret
source.quote: Suppose $\mathrm{Alg}_{\mathrm{On}}$ has a Hellinger regret bound $\overline{\mathrm{Reg}}_{\mathrm{On}}^{\mathrm{H}}( \mathcal{Q}, T, \delta)$. Fix $\gamma > 0$. Then, for any $\delta \in (0,1)$, with probability at least $1-\delta$, $\mathrm{Reg}_T \leq T \cdot \max_{t=1}^T \mathcal{V}_{\gamma}(\hat{q}_t(x_t), p_t) + \gamma \cdot \overline{\mathrm{Reg}}_{\mathrm{On}}^{\mathrm{H}}(\mathcal{Q}, T, \delta)$.

results.notes: Meta-regret theorem; applies to any exploration rule. Regret defined via expected losses p_t^T L q*(x_t), i.e. conditional on realised sampling; probability over the oracle event.

bound.regime: T large enough that gamma > 16 k^2 beta^2

symbols.beta_w: max over action pairs of the sup-norm of global-observability witness functions
symbols.Reg_On: Hellinger regret bound of the online outcome estimation oracle, Reg_On^H(Q,T,delta)

conditions: online oracle with Hellinger regret bound Reg_On

source.label: corollary_regret_e2d_global
source.quote: Then, for any $\delta \in (0,1)$, and for any large enough $T$ that satisfies $\gamma > 16 k^2 \beta^2$ with $\gamma = ( T k \beta / \overline{\mathrm{Reg}}_{\mathrm{On}}^{\mathrm{H}}(\mathcal{Q}, T, \delta) )^{2/3}$, with probability of at least $1-\delta$, \edpm run with Alg~\ref{alg:explore-go} as the exploration rule satisfies, $\mathrm{Reg}_T \leq O( \sqrt[3]{T^2k^2\beta^2\overline{\mathrm{Reg}}_{\mathrm{On}}^{\mathrm{H}}(\mathcal{Q}, T, \delta) })$.

results.notes: For finite Q with Vovk's aggregating algorithm Reg_On = 2 log(|Q|/delta), giving O((T^2 k^2 beta^2 log|Q|)^(1/3)) (stated in text).

symbols.Reg_On: Hellinger regret bound of the online outcome estimation oracle, Reg_On^H(Q,T,delta)

conditions: locally observable, non-degenerate game without duplicate actions
online oracle with Hellinger regret bound Reg_On

source.label: corollary_regret_e2d_local
source.quote: Let Assumption~\ref{assumption_ono_degen} hold, and suppose in addition that the game is locally observable. Then, for any $\delta \in (0,1)$, with probability of at least $1-\delta$, \edpm run with Alg.~\ref{alg:explore-lo} ... satisfies $\mathrm{Reg}_T \leq O( \sqrt{ T \cdot m^2 k^2 \cdot \overline{\mathrm{Reg}}_{\mathrm{On}}^{\mathrm{H}}(\mathcal{Q}, T, \delta) } )$.

results.notes: For finite Q, Vovk gives O(sqrt(T m^2 k^2 log|Q|)).

symbols.beta_w: max sup-norm of global-observability witness functions
symbols.Reg_Off: Hellinger bound of the offline estimation oracle, Reg_Off^H(Q, T, delta/log T)

conditions: non-degenerate globally observable game without duplicate actions
Reg_Off assumed not to depend on sample size t
tuning: gamma_l = (C tau_l k beta / Reg_Off(Q, tau_l/2, delta/L))^(2/3), gamma_l > 16 k^2 beta^2

source.quote: For globally observable games, with $\gamma_{\ell} = (\frac{ C \cdot \tau_{\ell}\cdot k \beta}{\overline{\mathrm{Reg}}_{\mathrm{Off}}^{\mathrm{H}} (\mathcal{Q}, \tau_{\ell}/2, \delta/L)} )^{\frac{2}{3}}$ ..., $\widetilde{\mathrm{Reg}}_T \leq O( T^{\frac{2}{3}}\log^2(T) (k \beta )^{\frac{2}{3}} (\overline{\mathrm{Reg}}_{\mathrm{Off}}^{\mathrm{H}} (\mathcal{Q}, T , \delta/ \log (T)))^{\frac{1}{3}} )$

results.notes: Bound on regret averaged over i.i.d. contexts, holding with probability 1-delta over oracle events (from Theorem D.2 proof). Corollary statement itself does not restate the probability. The general epoch bound Theorem D.2 not recorded separately.

symbols.Reg_Off: Hellinger bound of the offline estimation oracle, Reg_Off^H(Q, T/2, delta/log T)

conditions: non-degenerate locally observable game without duplicate actions
Reg_Off assumed not to depend on sample size t
tuning: kappa = gamma_l/(8 k^2 m^2), mu = k
gamma_l = sqrt(D tau_l k^3 m^2 / Reg_Off(Q, tau_l/2, delta_l))

source.quote: For locally observable games, with $\gamma_{\ell}= \sqrt{\frac{ D \cdot \tau_{\ell}\cdot k^3 m^2 }{\overline{\mathrm{Reg}}_{\mathrm{Off}}^{\mathrm{H}} (\mathcal{Q}, \tau_{{\ell}}/2, \delta_{{\ell}})} }$ ..., $\widetilde{\mathrm{Reg}}_T = O( \log^2(T) \sqrt{T\cdot k^3 m^2 \overline{\mathrm{Reg}}_{\mathrm{Off}}^{\mathrm{H}} (\mathcal{Q}, T/2, \delta/\log(T) ) } )$

results.notes: Expected over i.i.d. contexts; high probability over oracle events per Theorem D.2. Note k^3 dependence (vs k^2 online).
